the structure of the human isoform of 6-phophofructo2-kinase/ fructose-2.6-bisphoshpatase (PFK2) has been determined and that this structure reveals the mechanism by which the hypoxia-inducing factor (HIF) regulates the activity of the enzyme.

we determined the crystal structure of PFKFB3, a key enzyme that enables cancerous cells to survive under severe hypoxic stress conditions, at 2.10 Angstroms resolution, and that we found that the structure is similar to those of PFKFB1 and PFKFB4, but the regulatory domains are in a different configuration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the human PFKFB3 isoform and its possible application to the development of a cancer therapeutic.
the structural basis of PFKFB3 activity and its regulation.
understanding the molecular architecture of PFKFB3, a crucial enzyme in the progression of cancers, and with providing a molecular scaffold for designing new cancer-therapeutics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hypoxia-induible isoform has a unique structural architecture and functional properties, which are different from those of the other PFKFB isoform structures, and which are likely to be responsible for its unique biological function in cancerous cells.
this is the first structure of the human hypoxia-induced PFKFB isoform, and the structure provides a solid basis for the design of cancer therapeutic molecules.
the hypoxia-inducing form of PFKFB3 has evolved its unique structural characteristics, which allow it to maintain a high activity of glycolytic flux even under severe hypoxia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hypoxia-inducing form of PFKFB3 has evolved to have a unique architecture that allows the cell to adapt to hypoxic conditions by enabling glycolysis even under severe hypoxia.

the hypoxic form of PFKFB3 has a more rigid active pocket of the kinase domain than the liver or testis form and an open active pocket of the bisphosphatase active pocket with a β-hairpinned N-terminal domain that secures binding of fructose 6-phosphate to slow down the release of the phosphoenzymes.
the crystal structure of PFKFB3 reveals a novel mechanism of the regulation of its fructose-2-phosphate 2-Pase activity and provides a molecular scaffold for designing novel anticancer therapeutics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crystal structure provides a molecular scaffold for rational design of new anticancer drugs that target PFKFB3.
